note: Every statement in internal/ that no test executes. An entry states why the block cannot be executed, never that nobody has got round to it: a missing test is a missing test, and belongs in a test file. Enforced by internal/coverageaudit's own test, which fails both when an unlisted statement becomes uncovered and when a listed one becomes covered. Keys are file, enclosing function and the block's own source text, so a line moving does not invalidate an entry but a rewrite does.

exclusions.statement: panic(fmt.Sprintf("event: canonicalJSON: marshal string %q: %v", s, err))
exclusions.reason: json.Marshal of a Go string. The encoder rejects only invalid UTF-8 in byte slices and unsupported kinds; a string is neither, and is re-encoded with invalid runes replaced rather than refused.

exclusions.statement: return event.Envelope{}, fmt.Errorf("fills: marshal fill payload: %w", err)
exclusions.reason: json.Marshal of the payload the Validate immediately above has just accepted. The encoder refuses exactly one thing this payload could hold — a NaN or an infinity in a float64 field — and that payload's own Validate tests every one of its float fields for finiteness before this line is reached. Nothing else in it (strings, ints, slices of those, time.Time) has a failing encoding at all. Reachable the moment a float field is added without a finiteness check beside it.

exclusions.statement: return fmt.Errorf("registry: encode the run: %w", err)
exclusions.reason: json.MarshalIndent of the entry the Validate immediately above has just accepted. The encoder refuses exactly one thing this entry could hold — a NaN or an infinity in a float64 field — and every one of the ten float64 fields in event.ConfigurationPayload (including the nested NotionalAccountConfig and CommissionConfig) is tested for finiteness by ConfigurationPayload.Validate, which Entry.Validate calls. Nothing else in the entry (strings, a uint32, a uint64, two time.Time values) has a failing encoding at all. Reachable the moment a float field is added to the payload without a finiteness check beside it.

exclusions.statement: return fmt.Errorf("journal: encode line: %w", err)
exclusions.reason: writeLine has two callers, a Header and a Record. A Header is strings, a uint32 and two time.Time values. A Record adds an event.Envelope, whose only field that could fail to encode is the raw-JSON payload — and Write has already required every entry's envelope to pass event.Envelope.Validate, which refuses a payload that is not valid JSON.

exclusions.statement: return Unit{}, unrecognisedModeError(in.Mode)
exclusions.reason: RiskAtStop, called at the top of the same function, already rejects every Mode but the two the switch handles. The arm is kept so that declaring a third Mode without extending this switch fails closed rather than silently sizing nothing (ADR 0003).

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf("strategy: instrument %q: add fill %q is %s but campaign %q is %s; the add must be in the campaign's own direction (FillPayload.Direction is the position's direction, not the order's buy/sell side)", fill.InstrumentID, fill.FillID, fill.Direction, campaign.campaignID, campaign.direction)
exclusions.reason: The Baseline is long-only: event.DirectionLong is the only direction FillPayload.Validate, TradeProposalPayload.Validate and CampaignOpenedPayload.Validate accept, and a Campaign's own direction is only ever set from an accepted fill. The comparison therefore cannot differ today. It is kept, not deleted, because the rule it states is about reconciliation rather than about the payload contract — a fill in the opposite direction is a different position, not a variant of the same one — and it must already be in place on the day shorts are added rather than being remembered then. This entry becomes reachable, and must move to a test, the moment a second direction is accepted anywhere.

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf( "strategy: applied %d drawdown steps in one account snapshot observation without terminating; this indicates a defect in the drawdown ladder, not a legitimate market condition", i)
exclusions.reason: The Drawdown Ladder's own asymptote check, a few statements above, refuses a ladder whose steps do not converge; with a converging ladder the loop terminates in at most as many steps as the ladder has rungs, far below the cap. Kept as a bound on memory so that a future change to either the ladder or the asymptote check cannot silently reintroduce an unbounded append.

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf("strategy: built invalid notional account rebased payload: %w", err)
exclusions.reason: Validate on a payload this function assembled, field by field, from figures that had already passed sizing's own guards, the configuration's Validate, or an accepted payload's Validate. Where the validator re-derives a figure rather than range-checking it, the producer above forms it in the SAME expression order, so the two agree bit for bit rather than approximately (docs/development.md's fusion rule). If that ever stops holding this guard fires, becomes covered, and the audit reports this entry as stale rather than letting it pass.

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf("strategy: marshal notional account rebased payload: %w", err)
exclusions.reason: json.Marshal of the payload the Validate immediately above has just accepted. The encoder refuses exactly one thing this payload could hold — a NaN or an infinity in a float64 field — and that payload's own Validate tests every one of its float fields for finiteness before this line is reached. Nothing else in it (strings, ints, slices of those, time.Time) has a failing encoding at all. Reachable the moment a float field is added without a finiteness check beside it.

exclusions.statement: return r.decline(bar, input, signalID, event.DeclineReasonNNotReady, fmt.Sprintf("n is not a usable volatility reading (n %v); no unit can be sized from it", n), 0, 0)
exclusions.reason: sizeUnit has one call site, inside the branch guarded by `ready := nReady && entryChannelReady`, so nReady is always true here. The guard stays because it is what stops a division by an unusable N if that Tier gate ever changes, and 'it cannot happen here' is not a reason to divide by it.

exclusions.statement: return "", fmt.Errorf("strategy: sizing mode %q is not a recognised sizing mode; failing closed rather than sizing a position under an unknown principle (ADR 0003)", mode)
exclusions.reason: ConfigurationPayload.Validate accepts only event.SizingModeVolatilityNormalised and event.SizingModeFixedRiskAtStop, and a Reducer reads its mode from nowhere else. The guard is kept so that declaring a third Mode without extending the switch fails closed rather than sizing a position under an unknown principle (ADR 0003).
